parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no documented police/border targeting, no facility or custody rule, and same-sex conduct is lawful — so there is no tier-1 universal exposure and no tier-2 organised targeting to deduct for. But the positives are almost entirely silence: the dossier expressly leaves border document handling, facilities, custody and street-level service treatment unaddressed, so absence of evidence cannot be read as safety. Against that, the institutional climate is unfavourable and documented: gender recognition conditional on surgery, no nonbinary recognition, no GI anti-discrimination or hate-crime provision (2024 amendment blocked), entrenched marriage exclusion, mobilised religious opposition, 12% approval in regional polling, and no remedy mechanism a visitor could use. One subnational third-gender tradition is a single local point the dossier warns not to generalise. Net: above the documented-universal-exposure tier (0.45), below tiers with documented acceptance or working remedies (0.65+).
